question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[\sqrt{X}],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}, & x\ge 1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)=\sqrt{x}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[\sqrt{X}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{1/2}\cdot {x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{-3/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-2{x}^{-1/2}]}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =0-(-2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
